Hypotheses:
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

nda-11: No reverse engineering - The document doesn't mention reverse engineering anywhere. NotMentioned.

nda-16: Return of confidential information - No mention of destroying or returning Confidential Information upon termination. Segment 29 discusses termination but doesn't mention return/destruction. NotMentioned.

nda-15: No licensing - The Agreement mentions access to Confidential Information (segment 7) but doesn't explicitly state that no rights/license are granted. NotMentioned.

nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement - No mention of keeping the Agreement's existence confidential. NotMentioned.

nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information - Segment 3 lists Confidential Information including "services, customers etc." which are non-technical. So Confidential Information includes non-technical information, contradicting "shall only include technical information." Contradiction, evidence [3].

nda-1: Explicit identification - Segment 7 says "Confidential Information as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing." This suggests not all CI needs to be expressly identified (verbal, not reduced in writing allowed). So "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified" is contradicted. Contradiction, evidence [7].

nda-19: Survival of obligations - Segment 29 says term continues until termination or premises relocated/vacated/abandoned. No explicit survival clause. NotMentioned.

nda-12: Permissible development of similar information - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information - Segment 7: "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing." This entails that CI may include verbally conveyed info. Entailment, evidence [7]. Also segment 3 defines CI broadly but 7 is key.

nda-18: No solicitation - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-7: Sharing with third-parties - Segment 10 says no sharing with any Third Party. So hypothesis "may share some CI with some third-parties" is contradicted. Contradiction, evidence [10].

nda-17: Permissible copy - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure - Segment 11 says Recipient must prevent disclosure even if authorized/directed under law, without express permission of Discloser. This implies permission needed, but does it require notice? "without the express permission of the Discloser" - to get permission, Recipient would need to notify. Hmm. This could be entailment or contradiction. The hypothesis says "shall notify Disclosing Party in case required by law to disclose." Segment 11 requires express permission before disclosure under law. This arguably entails notification (must seek permission). But strictly, it says prevent disclosure even if required by law, without express permission. This is stronger than notice. I'd lean Entailment with evidence [11]? Actually it says "prevent and protect... from disclosure... even if authorized or directed under any law, without the express permission of the Discloser." This implies that if required by law, Recipient still cannot disclose without express permission - which requires contacting Discloser. Many NDA datasets label this as Entailment for notice on compelled disclosure when permission is required. I'll say Entailment, evidence [11].

nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-5: Sharing with employees - Segment 10 prohibits sharing with any Third Party. Are employees third parties? Typically employees aren't third parties. The document doesn't mention employees. NotMentioned.

nda-4: Limited use - Segment 10: "Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" - actually it says no use at all! "No Use: Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way or under any circumstances share the same..." Wait, that says not to use in any way. The hypothesis says "shall not use CI for any purpose other than purposes stated in Agreement." If Recipient cannot use CI at all, then it cannot use it for other purposes - entailment (a total prohibition includes prohibition of other-purpose use). But also segment 5 mentions Purpose of supply/installation of CCTV. Segment 15 allows access to layout plan for carrying out the contract. Hmm. Segment 10 says not to use in any way. The hypothesis is a weaker statement - not using for purposes other than stated ones. If no use is allowed at all, then certainly no use for other purposes. Entailment, evidence [10]. Possibly [5] too for purpose statement. I'll use [10] primarily, maybe [5,10].

Let me verify a few with human_feedback. I'll check nda-2 with [3], nda-1 with [7], nda-8 with [11], nda-4 with [10], nda-7 with [10], nda-3 with [7].
